# Interfaces

<!-- purpose: Where Interfaces files live, the kinds they hold and every key they accept -->

*This page is generated from SWCraft's own definitions, and describes the version you have installed.*

Port interfaces. Three element kinds discriminated by `kind`: `sender_receiver` (typed data elements), `client_server` (operations with typed, directional arguments) and `external_interface` (a stub for an interface declared outside the project, carrying the reference the source made to it).

One file per `interface`, in `interfaces/` under the model root, named after its `name` and ending in `.yaml`. Where that file name is already taken by another element's file — compared without regard to case — the file gets the nearest free `~1`, `~2`, … instead; the element is identified by the `name` inside the file, never by its file name.

A file of this layer is one of 3 kinds — `sender_receiver`, `client_server`, `external_interface` — chosen by its `kind` key.

## `sender_receiver` { #sender_receiver }

<!-- purpose: Writing `sender_receiver` files in Interfaces: each key, its type and default -->

A sender-receiver interface: the set of typed data elements exchanged over a port. Discriminated from `client_server` by `kind: sender_receiver`; it must declare at least one data element.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The interface's identity; the file is named from it (`interfaces/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across every interface kind, must not be blank, and immutable. |
| `kind` | string, one of `sender_receiver` | yes | — | The discriminator that selects this interface kind; always `sender_receiver`. |
| `data_elements` | a list of `data_element` blocks | yes | — | The typed data elements exchanged over the interface, addressed by `name`, which must be unique inside the interface. Must not be empty. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the interface. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
| `package` | string | no | absent | The one sub-package of `/PortInterfaces` this sender-receiver interface is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the sender-receiver interface and the forms generated from it and every reference to it take `/PortInterfaces/{package}/`. Absent means `/PortInterfaces` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/PortInterfaces/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/PortInterfaces` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule. |
| `is_service` | boolean | no | `false` | Whether the interface is a service interface, AUTOSAR's `isService`: one meant for communication with basic software services rather than between application components. Written into the generated ARXML as the interface's `IS-SERVICE`, which states `false` when the model is silent, and left out of the file while it is `false`. A composition may not declare a boundary port typed by a service interface, and the two ends of a connector or a delegation must agree on it. |
| `satisfies` | a list of string values | no | `[]` | The requirements this interface satisfies, each as the requirement's `id` and, after `@`, the version the link was confirmed for (`REQ-12@3`); a bare `id` is reported as a version not stated, and a version other than the requirement's as a link needing confirmation. A link is added or removed, never edited in place. A link here does not justify the components using the interface. It allocates no ASIL to anything. |

## `client_server` { #client_server }

<!-- purpose: Writing `client_server` files in Interfaces: each key, its type and default -->

A client-server interface: the set of operations a server port offers and a client port calls, each with its typed, directional arguments. Discriminated by `kind: client_server`; it must declare at least one operation.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The interface's identity; the file is named from it (`interfaces/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across every interface kind, must not be blank, and immutable. |
| `kind` | string, one of `client_server` | yes | — | The discriminator that selects this interface kind; always `client_server`. |
| `operations` | a list of `operation` blocks | yes | — | The operations a server port offers and a client port calls, addressed by `name`, which must be unique inside the interface. Must not be empty. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the interface. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
| `package` | string | no | absent | The one sub-package of `/PortInterfaces` this client-server interface is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the client-server interface and every reference to it take `/PortInterfaces/{package}/`. Absent means `/PortInterfaces` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/PortInterfaces/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/PortInterfaces` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule. |
| `is_service` | boolean | no | `false` | Whether the interface is a service interface, AUTOSAR's `isService`: one meant for communication with basic software services rather than between application components. Written into the generated ARXML as the interface's `IS-SERVICE`, which states `false` when the model is silent, and left out of the file while it is `false`. A composition may not declare a boundary port typed by a service interface, and the two ends of a connector or a delegation must agree on it. |
| `satisfies` | a list of string values | no | `[]` | The requirements this interface satisfies, each as the requirement's `id` and, after `@`, the version the link was confirmed for (`REQ-12@3`); a bare `id` is reported as a version not stated, and a version other than the requirement's as a link needing confirmation. A link is added or removed, never edited in place. A link here does not justify the components using the interface. It allocates no ASIL to anything. |

## `external_interface` { #external_interface }

<!-- purpose: Writing `external_interface` files in Interfaces: each key, its type and default -->

A stub for a port interface declared outside the project: an ARXML export referenced it and declared it nowhere. It carries that reference, `external_ref` and `external_dest`, verbatim, and the names of the members the project's ports use — `operations` on a client-server stub, `data_elements` on a sender-receiver one — and nothing of their content. A port naming it is emitted with that reference, and no interface is generated for it. Discriminated by `kind: external_interface`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The stub's identity; the file is named from it (`interfaces/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across every interface kind, must not be blank, and immutable. It is the name a port's `interface` gives; the reference the port is emitted with is `external_ref`. |
| `kind` | string, one of `external_interface` | yes | — | The discriminator that selects this interface kind; always `external_interface`. |
| `external_ref` | string | no | `""` | The AUTOSAR path the source's interface reference carried, verbatim: the interface's full path in the file that declares it. Written back unchanged into every port that names the stub. `check-model` reports a blank or malformed one. |
| `external_dest` | string | no | `""` | The `DEST` the source's interface reference carried, verbatim: one of the eight port interface values the AUTOSAR schema enumerates, `CLIENT-SERVER-INTERFACE`, `SENDER-RECEIVER-INTERFACE`, `MODE-SWITCH-INTERFACE`, `NV-DATA-INTERFACE`, `PARAMETER-INTERFACE`, `TRIGGER-INTERFACE` or the abstract `DATA-INTERFACE` and `PORT-INTERFACE`. A concrete value names the interface's kind, which a connector or a delegation is checked against; an abstract one does not. `check-model` reports any other value. |
| `operations` | a list of string values | no | `[]` | The names of the operations of the external interface that the project's ports use, each the last segment of a member path directly under `external_ref`. Names only: nothing of a member's content is held. Listed only on a stub whose `external_dest` is `CLIENT-SERVER-INTERFACE`; a name listed twice, ignoring case, or a blank one is refused. A member a port's runnable, event or com-spec entry names must be listed here. An empty list is left out of the file. |
| `data_elements` | a list of string values | no | `[]` | The names of the data elements of the external interface that the project's ports use, each the last segment of a member path directly under `external_ref`. Names only: nothing of a member's content is held. Listed only on a stub whose `external_dest` is `SENDER-RECEIVER-INTERFACE`; a name listed twice, ignoring case, or a blank one is refused. A member a port's runnable, event or com-spec entry names must be listed here. An empty list is left out of the file. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the stub. An external stub emits no element, so it reaches no generated artifact. |
| `satisfies` | a list of string values | no | `[]` | The requirements this interface stub satisfies, each as the requirement's `id` and, after `@`, the version the link was confirmed for (`REQ-12@3`); a bare `id` is reported as a version not stated, and a version other than the requirement's as a link needing confirmation. A link is added or removed, never edited in place. A link here does not justify the components using the interface. It allocates no ASIL to anything. |

## Blocks used inside those files { #blocks-used-inside-those-files }

<!-- purpose: The blocks nested inside Interfaces files, which are not files of their own -->

These are not files of their own: each appears as a block inside an element of this layer.

### `data_element` { #data_element }

<!-- purpose: Writing `data_element` blocks in Interfaces: each key, its type and default -->

One data element of a sender-receiver interface: a name, the declared data type it carries (`application_type` for an application data type, `implementation_type` for an implementation data type), an optional `init` value it starts from, and an optional `asil` for the safety integrity level of the information it carries.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The data element's identity inside its interface; unique among the interface's data elements and immutable. |
| `application_type` | string, the `name` of [application_types](application_types.md) | no | absent | The name of the declared application data type this data element carries, an element of the `application_types` layer: an application type, an enumeration, a record or an array. Exactly one of `application_type` and `implementation_type` is set. |
| `implementation_type` | string, the `name` of [implementation_types](implementation_types.md) | no | absent | The name of the declared implementation data type this data element carries, an element of the `implementation_types` layer: a value type, a reference type, an implementation record, an implementation array, a pointer or an external data type stub. Exactly one of `application_type` and `implementation_type` is set. |
| `init` | a scalar, a list, or a mapping, which may nest | no | absent | The value this data element starts from, where the design fixes one. Optional, and its shape follows the element's own declared type: a plain scalar for an application type, for a value type or for a reference type (judged against the type at the end of its chain), the literal's own name for an enumeration, the name of one of the table's entries for a value type or a reference type that references a table (itself or along its chain), a map keyed by exactly the declared field or element names for a record or an implementation record, and a list of exactly the declared length for an array or an implementation array. A pointer takes none. A value the declared type cannot hold is reported as a model error rather than converted. A port of a component may state a value of its own for the element in its `com_specs`, which takes precedence on that port. |
| `asil` | string, one of `QM`, `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, `QM(A)`, `QM(B)`, `QM(C)`, `QM(D)`, `A(B)`, `A(C)`, `A(D)`, `B(B)`, `B(C)`, `B(D)`, `C(C)`, `C(D)`, `D(D)` | no | absent | The safety integrity level of the information this element carries: `QM`, `A`, `B`, `C` or `D`, or a decomposed `X(Y)` such as `B(D)` — the thirteen spellings the AUTOSAR Safety Extensions list — where `Y` is the level before decomposition. Every rule ranks by `X`; one rule, `trace.decomposition-context-mismatch`, compares a requirement's `(Y)` with the level its parent requirement had before decomposition. The level sits on the element rather than on the interface or on the type, so one interface may carry a rated element beside an unrated one. Absent when none is allocated; a written `QM`, `QM(Y)` included, declares that none is — ISO 26262-1 calls QM not an ASIL, so it is not the lowest level — and is read as a declaration rather than as an absence. A component providing an element rated above its own level is reported, and so is one requiring an element rated below its own level unless the port declares a measure for that element. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the data element. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
| `sw_impl_policy` | string, one of `standard`, `queued` | no | absent | AUTOSAR's `swImplPolicy` for this element: `standard`, or `queued` for an element whose values the receiver queues rather than overwrites. Absent means `standard`, and nothing is written for it; a stated value is written into the generated ARXML as the element's `SW-IMPL-POLICY`. A queued element is sent and received through queued com-specs, a `require` port reading one names its `queue_length` in `com_specs`, and a by-value read may not take one. |
| `sw_calibration_access` | string, one of `not_accessible`, `read_only`, `read_write` | no | absent | AUTOSAR's `swCalibrationAccess` for this element: how a measurement and calibration tool may reach it, `not_accessible`, `read_only` or `read_write`. Absent means `not_accessible`, and nothing is written for it; a stated value is written into the generated ARXML as the element's `SW-CALIBRATION-ACCESS`. An element whose `sw_impl_policy` is `queued` supports `not_accessible` only. |

### `operation` { #operation }

<!-- purpose: Writing `operation` blocks in Interfaces: each key, its type and default -->

One operation of a client-server interface: a name and its ordered, typed, directional arguments; an operation may take no arguments at all.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The operation's identity inside its interface; unique among the interface's operations and immutable. |
| `arguments` | a list of `argument` blocks | no | `[]` | The operation's ordered arguments, addressed by `name`, which must be unique inside the operation. May be empty. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the operation. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |

### `argument` { #argument }

<!-- purpose: Writing `argument` blocks in Interfaces: each key, its type and default -->

One argument of a client-server operation: its name, the direction data flows through it, and the declared data type it carries (`application_type` for an application data type, `implementation_type` for an implementation data type).

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The argument's identity inside its operation; unique among the operation's arguments and immutable. |
| `direction` | string, one of `in`, `out`, `inout` | yes | — | The direction data flows through the argument: `in` from client to server, `out` from server to client, `inout` both ways. |
| `application_type` | string, the `name` of [application_types](application_types.md) | no | absent | The name of the declared application data type this argument carries, an element of the `application_types` layer: an application type, an enumeration, a record or an array. Exactly one of `application_type` and `implementation_type` is set. |
| `implementation_type` | string, the `name` of [implementation_types](implementation_types.md) | no | absent | The name of the declared implementation data type this argument carries, an element of the `implementation_types` layer: a value type, a reference type, an implementation record, an implementation array, a pointer or an external data type stub. Exactly one of `application_type` and `implementation_type` is set. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the argument. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
